<p class="kicker">The short answer</p>

## Promising enough to try as a helper

We set out to answer one question first: is a free model on your own computer good enough to take routine work off a paid AI coding plan? For reading and everyday coding, the answer looks like yes.

- **Coding:** it fixed 360 of 500 real bugs (72.00%) on SWE-bench Verified, working on its own with a terminal and tests.
- **Careful reasoning:** it answered just over half (54.55%) of 198 expert science questions on GPQA Diamond.

Each score belongs to its own test. The tests measure different things, so we never add them together or say the model is "better" at one than the other.

</section>

<section class="reader-section warm" id="what-results-show" aria-label="What the results show" data-step>
<span class="testpoint" data-testpoint aria-hidden="true">02</span>

<p class="kicker">What the results show</p>

## A capable helper for routine work

A helper does not have to be the smartest model in the room. It has to handle the routine parts well: reading files, finding the right code, and making ordinary fixes. The paid model can then check the work and take the hard calls.

SWE-bench Verified is the closest of our two tests to that job. Each task is a real bug report from an open-source project, and the fix only counts when the project's own tests pass. Fixing about 7 in 10 of them on one local machine is a strong sign the helper can do real work.

GPQA Diamond checks a different skill: careful reasoning on hard questions that are difficult to look up. A result just over half tells us the model can reason, but it is not a top expert on the hardest problems.

</section>

<section class="reader-section cool" id="not-shown-yet" aria-label="What the results do not show yet" data-step>
<span class="testpoint" data-testpoint aria-hidden="true">03</span>

<p class="kicker">Not shown yet</p>

## What these results do not prove

- **Savings.** These tests measure skill, not savings. We have not yet measured how much of a real plan a helper saves. That is the next experiment.
- **That MinionS applies to coding.** The Stanford MinionS study cut cloud costs about 5.7 times while keeping 97.9% of the cloud model's accuracy. But it asked questions about long documents, not coding, and it used different models.
- **A ranking against cloud models.** Today's top cloud models report higher scores on both tests, but they were tested with different tools, settings, and scoring. We show those scores as context, never as an exact gap.
- **Every setup.** Our results apply to this exact model, engine, and settings. A different build, runtime, or setting is a new test.
- **A clean-room test.** Both benchmarks are public, so the model may have seen some of the questions during training.

</section>

## What it takes to run

<dl class="readouts">
  <div><dt>Machine</dt><dd><strong>128 GB Mac</strong><span>Everything ran locally; nothing was sent to the cloud</span></dd></div>
  <div><dt>Writing speed</dt><dd><strong>64.13 tokens/s</strong><span>Average on the science test</span></dd></div>
  <div><dt>Science test run time</dt><dd><strong>2 h 25 m</strong><span>198 questions, one at a time, about 44 s each</span></dd></div>
  <div><dt>Coding test run time</dt><dd><strong>Not measured</strong><span>No reviewed timing for the coding run yet</span></dd></div>
</dl>

One lesson from the coding run: the test machine locked up twice when the Splash engine's memory use kept growing. We capped its memory at 48 GiB, which limits only its cache, and the run finished. The result record lists this and every other change from the standard setup.

[See the coding run's full record](/splash-evals/dashboard/swe-bench-verified/)

## Measuring real savings

We are building a delegation plugin that lets Claude Code and Codex hand routine work to a local helper, and we plan to open-source it. Early experiments are under way. Next we will:

1. Test the Unsloth build of Qwen3.8 against this Splash build and keep the better one.
2. Test low-cost models on Ollama Cloud as another kind of helper.
3. Measure how much plan usage each helper actually saves on real coding work.

Those results will live on a new delegation bench site. This site is its first chapter.

[See how we tested](/splash-evals/methodology/) · [Check the sources](/splash-evals/sources/)
